ai.title: Retire tool used funnel event and add agentic ads commitment constant
ai.summary: The agentic ads funnel vocabulary in the common package retires the tool used postback event, moving it into the retired list and removing it from the repeating and postback event sets so only account creation remains for advertiser postbacks. Simultaneously, the freebuff ads constants file adds the agentic ads minimum monthly commitment constant set to 1.5 million cents, defining a floor for invoiced sponsored proposal contracts. The retired event stays in the main array to preserve Postgres enum ordering, while the new constant is currently a definition without a visible runtime reader in the diff.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/agentic-ad-events.ts`, the event `tool_used` is moved into `RETIRED_AGENTIC_FUNNEL_EVENT_TYPES` and removed from `AGENTIC_POSTBACK_EVENT_TYPES` and `REPEATING_AGENTIC_FUNNEL_EVENT_TYPES`. In `common/src/constants/freebuff-ads.ts`, the new export `AGENTIC_ADS_MIN_MONTHLY_COMMITMENT_CENTS` is defined with the value `1_500_000`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the consumer that enforces the new agentic ads minimum monthly commitment constant or the specific page that quotes it.

eli5.text: Freebuff stopped accepting self-reported usage signals from advertisers for sponsored coding tasks, shifting that verification to the platform's own internal checks. The company also defined a new minimum monthly spend floor for these specific ad contracts, a figure that is currently in place but not yet actively enforced by a visible system. This is an internal adjustment to how advertising performance is tracked and priced, so you will see no changes in your daily use of the coding assistant.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-account-prompt
entries.summary: CLI, Shared/Core changes across 3 file(s) (+78/−17).

ai.title: Sponsored sign-in now accepts typed replies and step status lines
ai.summary: The sponsored account step in the CLI and shared ad subsystem now supports free-text user replies instead of a hard 'No' option, with `labSignupReplyText` capping input to 500 characters and `labSignupRepliedNote` instructing the agent to act on the reply as data. In `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts`, two new exports, `sponsoredCurrentStep` and `sponsoredStepStatusLine`, provide a formatted 'Step N of M' status string for minimized proposal cards, falling back to an offer plan count when individual step states are not yet reported.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/ads/agentic-ad-lab-run.ts` removes `LAB_SIGNUP_NO` and `LAB_SIGNIN_CONNECT_NEXT` while adding `labSignupRepliedNote` and `labSignupReplyText`; concurrently, `common/src/ads/sponsored-proposal-view.ts` introduces `sponsoredCurrentStep` and `sponsoredStepStatusLine` to format step progress.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the UI consumer that renders the new `sponsoredStepStatusLine` output or the typed-reply input field.

changes.what: Replaced the binary sign-in confirmation with a typed-reply mechanism, adding `labSignupReplyText` and `labSignupRepliedNote` while removing `LAB_SIGNUP_NO` and `LAB_SIGNIN_CONNECT_NEXT`.
Added `sponsoredCurrentStep` and `sponsoredStepStatusLine` functions to derive a human-readable step progress string from proposal step states or an offer plan count.
Updated the sign-in prompt text in the terminal UI to instruct users to create an account or sign in in the browser tab, aligning with the new one-line question format.

eli5.text: When the assistant pauses during a sponsored setup to ask you to sign in, you can now type a free-form message instead of only choosing between a confirmation and a decline. This allows you to explain a specific problem or request further help directly to the assistant. Additionally, a new progress line now appears on minimized sponsored task cards, showing exactly which step of the process is currently active. These changes affect anyone using the free coding assistant who accepts a sponsored offer, making the sign-in step more flexible and the task progress clearer.

entries.title: SDK update: sponsored-runtimes
entries.summary: SDK changes across 1 file(s) (+150/−49).

ai.title: Redirect sponsored runtime probe Python detection to Xcode CLT
ai.summary: The `SPONSORED_RUNTIME_PROBE_SCRIPT` in the SDK sponsored runtimes module now explicitly avoids the macOS system Python shim at `/usr/bin/python3`. When the probe detects a `python3` or `python` binary located at `/usr/bin/` on a Darwin host, it resolves the actual interpreter path using `xcode-select -p` and executes `--version` against that path instead. This prevents the probe from triggering the macOS Command Line Tools installer prompt during sponsored agent sandbox initialization. A new test suite verifies that the script correctly skips the shim when the developer Python is missing and reports availability when the CLT-provided binary is executable.
ai.evidence: The diff in `sdk/src/tools/sponsored-runtimes.ts` modifies `SPONSORED_RUNTIME_PROBE_SCRIPT` to intercept `python3` and `python` calls pointing to `/usr/bin/` on Darwin, redirecting execution to the Xcode Command Line Tools path resolved by `xcode-select -p`, and adds corresponding tests in `sdk/src/__tests__/sponsored-runtimes.test.ts`.

eli5.text: When Freebuff runs a sponsored task on a Mac, it now checks for Python in a specific way to avoid accidentally popping up the system's software installer. This is an internal safety check that runs quietly before these sponsored tasks begin. You will not see any difference in your day-to-day use of the app, and no new features are available from this update.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: freebuff-topups
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+8/−1).

ai.title: Add postpaid collection tier constants for payment history
ai.summary: Four new constants define the postpaid collection tiers in the shared placements module, allowing the system to collect earlier until the advertiser has established a payment history. The mature threshold is set to 20000 cents while the initial threshold is 2500 cents, with minimum requirements of 2 successful collections and 14 days of history to establish trust. These constants support the transition from the previous single $100 threshold sweep to payment-history based threshold sweeps.
ai.evidence: The diff adds four new exports to `common/src/constants/freebuff-topups.ts`: `AD_POSTPAID_MATURE_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD_CENTS` (20_000), `AD_POSTPAID_INITIAL_COLLECTION_THRESHOLD_CENTS` (2_500), `AD_POSTPAID_COLLECTION_MIN_SUCCESSES` (2), and `AD_POSTPAID_COLLECTION_MIN_HISTORY_DAYS` (14), alongside a doc comment update referencing 'payment-history threshold sweeps'.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the runtime consumer of these new constants or how the collection logic specifically utilizes the history days and success counts.

eli5.text: The system now uses two different spending checkpoints for advertisers who pay by credit card: a lower, earlier limit for new accounts and a higher limit for those with a proven payment record. To earn the higher limit, an advertiser must have at least two successful billings over a two-week period. This is an internal rule for managing ad accounts, so it does not affect your daily use of the coding tool or your personal data limits.
